brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Two keyhole hangers on the back faces of the outer cells, which line up flat for mounting on a wall. The middle cell hangs from them through joint bolts. The configurator doesn't check how much weight they can carry.
Three full-depth bins: bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0 and bin:2,-1,0.
hex-acc-keyhole accessories accessory:0#0,0#2 and accessory:0#2,-1#2. They hook onto screws already in the wall.

finish.summary: I built a 3-cell wall-hung spice rack. It has three full-depth bins and hangs from two keyhole hangers. Hex cells can't sit in a straight row with a flat back, so the cells are set in a shallow V. The two outer cells, (0,0) and (2,-1), have their slot-2 faces in line with each other (that side goes against the wall), and each of those faces carries a keyhole hanger. The middle cell (1,0) touches both and sits one half-step forward. It is bolted to the two outer cells with joint bolts and has no hanger of its own. All other open faces have end caps. check_build passes with no rule issues, and the mesh-collision check reads clear. The catalog has no spice-jar props, so I didn't add any. The configurator checks fit only: it can't say how much weight the hangers or plastic will hold.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
